stage.name: Grammar Foundations
stage.description: The sentence patterns behind everyday Urdu: pronouns and 'to be', gender and agreement, possession and family, numbers, present-tense verbs, and talking about likes, needs and feelings.

units.title: Me, You & "To Be"
units.description: Pronouns, ہونا (to be) and respectful speech

lessons.title: I Am, You Are
objectives: Use میں، تم، آپ as subjects
Match each pronoun with ہوں / ہو / ہیں
Notice that the verb comes last (subject-object-verb)
lessons.notes: Urdu sentences end with the verb. ہونا (to be) changes with the subject: میں ... ہوں، تم ... ہو، آپ ... ہیں. آپ always takes the plural form ہیں, even for one person - that is what makes it respectful.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: میں طالب علم ___ ۔

lessons.title: He, She, We & They
objectives: Use یہ (near) and وہ (far) for he, she, it and they
Use ہم (we) with ہیں
Use ہے (is) for one person or thing
lessons.notes: Urdu has no separate words for 'he' and 'she'. یہ means this person/thing nearby and وہ means that person/thing further away. Gender shows up in the verb and adjectives instead, which comes in Unit 2.

quiz.question: Which word points to someone far away?

lessons.title: Tum or Aap? Speaking Respectfully
objectives: Choose آپ for elders, strangers and anyone you respect
Use جی as a polite 'yes'
Address older people warmly as آنٹی، انکل، آپا، بھائی جان
lessons.notes: Respect is built into Urdu grammar. Use آپ with elders and people you don't know; تم is for close friends and children. Calling an older stranger آنٹی or انکل is normal and friendly. Elders often call younger people بیٹا (child) affectionately.

phrases.english: How are you? (respectful, to a man)
How are you? (casual, to a girl)

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: وعلیکم السلام بیٹا۔ تم کیسے ہو؟
dialogue.roman: wa alaikum assalam beta. tum kaise ho

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: جی، میں ٹھیک ہوں۔ آپ کیسی ہیں؟
dialogue.roman: jee, main theek hoon. aap kaisi hain

quiz.question: You meet your friend's grandmother. Which 'you' do you use?

lessons.title: Review: Meeting the Neighbours
objectives: Introduce yourself and someone with you
Use یہاں / وہاں (here / there)
Respond to خوش آمدید (welcome)
lessons.notes: This lesson recycles every pattern from the unit in one realistic conversation. Encourage learners to read the dialogue aloud in both roles.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: السلام علیکم! ہم نئے پڑوسی ہیں۔
dialogue.english: Hello! We are the new neighbours.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: میں سارہ ہوں، اور یہ میرا بھائی ہے۔
dialogue.roman: main Sara hoon, aur yeh mera bhai hai
dialogue.english: I am Sara, and this is my brother.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی۔
dialogue.roman: aap se mil kar khushi hui

units.title: Boy, Girl & Agreement
units.description: Noun gender, plurals, adjectives and colours

lessons.title: Masculine & Feminine
objectives: Know that every Urdu noun is masculine or feminine
Use the -ا (masculine) and -ی (feminine) ending pattern
Remember the common exception آدمی (man, masculine)
lessons.notes: Rule of thumb: nouns ending in ا are usually masculine (لڑکا) and nouns ending in ی are usually feminine (لڑکی). Exceptions exist - آدمی ends in ی but is masculine - so learn each noun together with its gender.

quiz.question: Nouns ending in ا (like لڑکا) are usually...
Nouns ending in ی (like لڑکی) are usually...
Which of these is masculine, even though it ends in ی?

lessons.title: One and Many (Plurals)
objectives: Make masculine -ا nouns plural with -ے
Make feminine -ی nouns plural with -یاں
Make other feminine nouns plural with -یں
lessons.notes: Plural patterns: لڑکا → لڑکے، کمرہ → کمرے (masc. -a → -e); لڑکی → لڑکیاں (fem. -i → -iyan); کتاب → کتابیں (fem. consonant → -ein). Masculine nouns ending in a consonant don't change: ایک دوست، دو دوست.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.english: The girls are in the room.

quiz.question: What is the plural of لڑکا?
What is the plural of کتاب?

lessons.title: Describing Things
objectives: Make -ا adjectives agree: اچھا (m), اچھی (f), اچھے (pl)
Place the adjective before the noun
Recognise adjectives that never change, like خوبصورت
lessons.notes: Adjectives ending in ا change to match the noun: اچھا لڑکا، اچھی لڑکی، اچھے لڑکے. Adjectives ending in anything else stay the same: خوبصورت لڑکا، خوبصورت لڑکی.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: میرا گھر بڑا اور خوبصورت ہے۔
dialogue.roman: mera ghar bara aur khoobsurat hai
dialogue.english: My house is big and beautiful.

lessons.title: Colours
objectives: Name six basic colours
Apply agreement to colour words (نیلا / نیلی)
Notice that لال and سفید never change
lessons.notes: Colours are adjectives, so the -ا ones agree: نیلا آسمان (sky, m) but نیلی گاڑی (car, f). لال and سفید don't end in ا, so they never change.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: آپ کا پسندیدہ رنگ کون سا ہے؟
dialogue.roman: aap ka pasandeeda rang kaun sa hai

quiz.question: Which colour word never changes form?

units.title: Mine, Yours & Family
units.description: Possessives, کا / کی / کے and family on both sides

lessons.title: My & Your
objectives: Use میرا / میری / میرے (my)
Use آپ کا / آپ کی (your, respectful)
Make the possessive agree with the thing owned
lessons.notes: The key idea: 'my' agrees with the thing you own, not with you. A woman says میرا گھر (house is masc.) and a man says میری کتاب (book is fem.).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: کیا یہ آپ کی کتاب ہے؟
dialogue.roman: kya yeh aap ki kitaab hai

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: جی نہیں، یہ میری کتاب نہیں ہے۔
dialogue.roman: jee nahin, yeh meri kitaab nahin hai
dialogue.english: No, this is not my book.

lessons.title: Whose Is It? (کا، کی، کے)
objectives: Show possession with کا / کی / کے ('s / of)
Ask 'whose?' with کس کا / کس کی
Choose کا / کی / کے by the gender of the thing owned
lessons.notes: کا / کی / کے work like English 's but come after the owner and agree with the thing owned: علی کا قلم (pen, m), علی کی کتاب (book, f), علی کے دوست (friends, pl).

lessons.title: Father's Side of the Family
objectives: Name grandparents and relatives on the father's side
Tell چچا (younger) and تایا (older) apart
Use respectful plural ہیں for elders
lessons.notes: Urdu has a separate word for each relative depending on which side of the family they're on. Father's side: دادا، دادی، چچا (father's younger brother)، تایا (father's elder brother)، پھوپھو (father's sister). Elders take the respectful plural: میرے دادا مہربان ہیں.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: یہ میرے دادا اور دادی ہیں۔
dialogue.roman: yeh mere dada aur dadi hain

lessons.title: Mother's Side & Siblings
objectives: Name grandparents and relatives on the mother's side
Talk about brothers, sisters and cousins
Ask how many siblings someone has
lessons.notes: Mother's side: نانا، نانی، ماموں (mother's brother)، خالہ (mother's sister). A useful contrast drill: دادا / نانا، دادی / نانی، پھوپھو / خالہ، چچا / ماموں.

phrases.urdu: میری خالہ لاہور میں رہتی ہیں۔
phrases.roman: meri khala Lahore mein rehti hain

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: آپ کے کتنے بہن بھائی ہیں؟
dialogue.roman: aap ke kitne behan bhai hain
dialogue.english: How many brothers and sisters do you have?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: میرا ایک بھائی اور دو بہنیں ہیں۔
dialogue.roman: mera ek bhai aur do behnein hain
dialogue.english: I have one brother and two sisters.

units.title: Numbers & Counting
units.description: 1-20, bigger numbers, prices and days of the week

lessons.title: One to Five
objectives: Count from 1 to 5
Say how many of something you have
Ask کتنے؟ (how many?)
lessons.notes: Numbers come before the noun and the noun goes plural from two upward: ایک کتاب، دو کتابیں. میرے پاس (lit. 'near me') is how Urdu says 'I have'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: آپ کے پاس کتنے قلم ہیں؟
dialogue.roman: aap ke paas kitne qalam hain
dialogue.english: How many pens do you have?

lessons.title: Six to Ten
objectives: Count from 6 to 10
Say your age with سال کا / سال کی
Ask عمر کتنی ہے؟ (how old?)
lessons.notes: Age agrees with the person: a boy says میں نو سال کا ہوں and a girl says میں نو سال کی ہوں - the same کا / کی agreement from Unit 3.

quiz.question: Which number comes right after چھ?
A girl says she is seven: میں سات سال ___ ہوں۔

lessons.title: Bigger Numbers & Prices
objectives: Ask a price with کتنے کا ہے؟
Understand a price in rupees
lessons.notes: Numbers 11-99 in Urdu are irregular, so learners memorise them gradually. Start with the ones used most in shops: 12, 15, 20, 50, 100, 1000. Full 11-20 list for practice: گیارہ، بارہ، تیرہ، چودہ، پندرہ، سولہ، سترہ، اٹھارہ، انیس، بیس.

quiz.question: How many months are in a year?

lessons.title: Days of the Week
objectives: Name the seven days
Ask and say what day it is
Understand that کل means both 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow'
lessons.notes: The week is often thought of as starting on پیر (Monday). جمعہ (Friday) is special in Muslim households - many families go to Friday prayers. کل means yesterday or tomorrow; the verb tense tells you which.

units.title: Everyday Actions
units.description: Verbs, the present tense, negatives and yes/no questions

lessons.title: Action Words
objectives: Recognise the dictionary form of verbs (ending in نا)
Learn seven high-frequency verbs
Combine a noun with a verb: پانی پینا
lessons.notes: Every Urdu verb's dictionary form ends in نا. Remove نا to get the stem: کھانا → کھا، پینا → پی. Learners will build every tense from that stem. Note: کھانا also means 'food'.

quiz.question: Urdu verbs in their dictionary form end in...

lessons.title: I Eat, I Drink
objectives: Form the present habitual: stem + تا / تی / تے + ہونا
Choose تا (male speaker) or تی (female speaker)
Talk about food and drink you have every day
lessons.notes: Present habitual = what you usually do. Stem + تا (m) / تی (f) / تے (plural or respectful) + ہونا: میں چائے پیتا ہوں (man), میں چائے پیتی ہوں (woman), ہم چائے پیتے ہیں. The speaker's gender matters, so learners should practise the form that matches them.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.english: What do you drink in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: میں چائے پیتی ہوں۔ اور آپ؟
dialogue.roman: main chai peeti hoon. aur aap

quiz.question: A girl says 'I drink': میں ___ ہوں۔

lessons.title: Not! Saying No
objectives: Make a sentence negative with نہیں before the verb
Drop ہے / ہوں in negative sentences, as speakers do
Use how-often words: ہمیشہ، کبھی کبھی، کبھی نہیں
lessons.notes: Put نہیں right before the verb: میں گوشت نہیں کھاتا. In everyday speech the final ہوں / ہے is usually dropped in negatives. کبھی نہیں (never) wraps around the verb: وہ کبھی دیر نہیں کرتی.

phrases.urdu: ہم ہمیشہ ساتھ کھانا کھاتے ہیں۔
phrases.roman: hum hamesha saath khana khate hain

quiz.question: Make it negative: میں گوشت ___ کھاتا۔

lessons.title: Yes/No Questions & My Day
objectives: Turn a statement into a question by adding کیا at the start
Name the parts of the day
Ask and answer about daily habits
lessons.notes: To ask a yes/no question, put کیا at the start and raise your voice at the end: آپ اردو بولتے ہیں → کیا آپ اردو بولتے ہیں؟ Here کیا doesn't mean 'what' - it just marks a question.

phrases.urdu: کیا وہ گھر پر کام کرتی ہے؟
phrases.roman: kya woh ghar par kaam karti hai

quiz.question: Turn into a question: آپ چائے پیتے ہیں۔

units.title: Likes, Needs & Feelings
units.description: مجھے ... پسند ہے، چاہیے، feelings and weather

lessons.title: I Like... (پسند)
objectives: Say what you like with مجھے ... پسند ہے
Ask what someone likes with آپ کو ... پسند ہے؟
Say what you don't like
lessons.notes: Urdu says 'to me, X is liked': مجھے آم پسند ہے. The person who likes takes کو (میں → مجھے، ہم → ہمیں، آپ → آپ کو). This same pattern is used for needs and feelings in the next lessons.

phrases.urdu: کیا آپ کو کرکٹ پسند ہے؟
phrases.roman: kya aap ko cricket pasand hai

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: آپ کو کون سا پھل پسند ہے؟
dialogue.roman: aap ko kaun sa phal pasand hai

lessons.title: I Need... (چاہیے)
objectives: Ask for things with مجھے ... چاہیے
Ask someone what they need
Shop for everyday items politely
lessons.notes: چاہیے uses the same 'to me' pattern as پسند: مجھے پانی چاہیے (I need water). It covers both 'need' and a polite 'want', which makes it one of the most useful words for travellers.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: مجھے دو روٹیاں اور دودھ چاہیے۔
dialogue.roman: mujhe do rotiyan aur doodh chahiye
dialogue.english: I need two rotis and milk.

quiz.question: What does مجھے چابی چاہیے mean?

lessons.title: How Do You Feel?
objectives: Describe feelings: happy, sad, tired, hungry, thirsty, ill
Make feeling adjectives agree (تھکا ہوا / تھکی ہوئی)
Ask what's wrong: کیا ہوا؟
lessons.notes: Feelings use ہونا with an adjective: میں خوش ہوں. Adjectives ending in ا agree with the speaker: a man is بھوکا، a woman is بھوکی. تھکا ہوا / تھکی ہوئی (tired) has two parts and both agree.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.urdu: کیا ہوا؟ تم اداس کیوں ہو؟
dialogue.roman: kya hua? tum udaas kyun ho
dialogue.english: What happened? Why are you sad?

quiz.question: A girl says 'I am tired': میں ___ ہوں۔

lessons.title: Weather & Review
objectives: Talk about the weather with گرمی، سردی، بارش
Say you feel hot or cold with مجھے ... لگ رہی ہے
Combine likes, needs and feelings in one conversation
lessons.notes: Weather words are nouns: آج گرمی ہے (lit. 'today there is heat'). Feeling hot or cold uses the 'to me' pattern again: مجھے سردی لگ رہی ہے. The dialogue recycles پسند، چاہیے and feelings from the whole unit.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: بارش ہو رہی ہے، اور سردی بھی ہے۔
dialogue.roman: baarish ho rahi hai, aur sardi bhi hai
dialogue.english: It's raining, and it's cold too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.urdu: مجھے بھی! مجھے بارش بہت پسند ہے۔
dialogue.roman: mujhe bhi! mujhe baarish bohat pasand hai
dialogue.english: Me too! I really like the rain.

quiz.question: 'It's very hot today': آج بہت ___ ہے۔
